h1:
Ranong Oysters
Giant Ones from the Kraburi Estuary
intro: Ranong gets eight months of rain and four of sun, and the fresh water of the Kraburi River meets the salty Andaman Sea right at the river mouth. That brackish mix is exactly what oysters love, so they grow big and meaty here, with a sweet, faintly salty flavour you rarely find elsewhere. We've picked spots that are actually open right now — raw oysters shucked at your table, the fried oyster omelette known as or suan, and floating sea farms where you eat with the Myanmar coast in view.

blocks.html: First-timers in Ranong usually think of the hot springs and Koh Phayam, but locals will tell you the one thing not to miss is the oysters. Ranong has several oyster farms strung along the Kraburi estuary and Klong La-un, where the oysters grow in clean brackish water and reach the size of your palm. The meat is bouncy and sweet with no fishy edge — great raw with a squeeze of lime, and just as good fried into or suan or tossed into a spicy salad.

In this guide we sort out which places are best for raw oysters, which do a killer fried oyster omelette, and which are floating farm rafts out at sea that you have to take a boat to reach. We've ranked them by freshness, value, and the real reviews we could find.

blocks.text: The Ranong oyster spots we picked

blocks.html: A lower spot on the list doesn't mean it's not good — each place has its own strength. Some are about the view, some about the price, some about how fresh the oysters are. Pick whatever fits your trip.

items.name: Keing Lay Restaurant
items.blurb: The place Ranong locals call the town's seafood legend, right on the waterfront at Pak Nam, looking across to Myanmar as the sun goes down. The raw oysters come piled high, big and bouncy, served with fried garlic, fried shallots and a punchy seafood dipping sauce. The catch comes straight from local fishermen every day.
items.meta: Pak Nam, Mueang district · ~10 km out of town · book a table for dinner to be safe

items.name: Farmer Boy Sea Raft
items.blurb: Dinner out at sea on a floating oyster-farm raft along Klong La-un. You take a boat out, then shuck oysters straight off the farm and eat them right there. The fisherman's tiffin set comes with lobster, oysters and green mussels, grilled over a view of Khao Fachi and the sunset. Only a few tables a day, so book ahead.
items.meta: Klong La-un · boat out to the farm · reservations 084-745-7527

items.name: Khun Lin Restaurant
items.blurb: A southern-Thai seafood spot in town that's been open more than 20 years, near the Raksawarin hot springs and only about 2 km from the centre. It does fresh oysters and or suan well, paired with bold southern dishes like khua kling and gaeng leuang. A good stop after a hot-spring soak.
items.meta: Chonla-u Rd, Khao Niwet, Mueang district · open daily 8:00–21:00

items.name: Somyot Pak Nam Seafood
items.blurb: A restaurant right on the river mouth with a clear water view. The standout is the oyster omelette, packed with big plump oysters, plus the raw oysters. Other dishes like fish-sauce-fried seabass and seafood tom yum come out fresh too. This is one locals bring people to often.
items.meta: On the river mouth, Pak Nam area, Mueang district

items.name: Riverside Restaurant, Kraburi
items.blurb: A spot on the Kraburi River in Kraburi district. The real draw is the big Kraburi river prawns, but the fresh oysters and seafood dishes are done well too. Quiet riverside setting, easy prices — a good stop if you're driving the Chumphon–Ranong route.
items.meta: 11/1 Moo 2, Plai Khlong Rd, Nam Chuet, Kraburi · tel 0-7789-1113 · opens Sat 09:00

items.name: Khun Lin (Kunlin) Restaurant
items.blurb: A seafood place known for jumbo-size ingredients piling up the plate — big crab, squid and prawns. The fresh oysters and or suan are done fresh too, and reviewers praise the freshness and the value for the portions. Great for a group ordering to share.
items.meta: Mueang Ranong district · check the day off before you go

items.name: Khao Fachi Restaurant
items.blurb: A seafood spot with a seaside setting in the La-un area, near the Khao Fachi viewpoint. Fish is weighed and sold by the kilo, and fresh oysters come with a full set of condiments. The draw is the sea view and the cool breeze — good for an early dinner that runs into the sunset.
items.meta: La-un area, near the Khao Fachi viewpoint
items.price: sold by weight, around 150 THB per 100g

items.name: Ranong market oyster stalls
items.blurb: If you'd rather buy fresh oysters to eat yourself or fry up or suan back at your place, the stalls in the municipal market and the seafood shops around Pak Nam sell shucked fresh oysters by the 100g or the kilo — cheaper than ordering at a sit-down restaurant. You can pick the big plump ones yourself, and ask for dipping sauce and lime to go.
items.meta: Ranong municipal market / Pak Nam stalls · go in the morning for fresher oysters
items.price: shucked fresh oysters from around 120–200 THB per 100g

blocks.title: How to eat oysters safely and well
blocks.html: For raw oysters, pick a place with quick turnover and good chilling — the meat should be clear with no sour, off smell. If your stomach isn't tough, order them fried as or suan or steamed instead of raw; you'll feel better about it. A squeeze of fresh lime right before eating cuts any fishiness and rounds out the flavour.

blocks.text: Raw, fried as or suan, or in a salad — which is best

blocks.html: Ranong oysters are big enough to eat several ways. If they're genuinely fresh, try them raw first to get the full sweetness, then move on to the cooked versions.

items: Raw oysters — shucked onto a plate with a squeeze of lime, eaten with fried garlic, fried shallots, pickled garlic and seafood dipping sauce, for the full sweet, bouncy hit.

Or suan (fried oyster omelette) — fried with batter and egg, crisp outside and soft inside, with big bouncy oysters in the batter, topped with Sriracha chilli sauce. A dish even people wary of raw food can enjoy.
Oyster salad (yum) — tossed with lemongrass, shallots, sliced kaffir lime leaf, chilli and lime, a sharp spicy hit that cuts the richness. Great with drinks.
Steamed or baked oysters — steamed with soy and ginger, or baked with garlic butter, for anyone who wants something soft and hot.

blocks.text: When to go for Ranong oysters

blocks.html: Farmed oysters are available year-round, but in the dry season from around November to April the sea is calm and the farms produce more steadily. The water is smooth too, which makes it easier to take a boat out to the floating farm rafts. In the rainy season Ranong gets heavy downpours, and the sea rafts may close on some days — so if you're planning a boat trip, always call the place to check first.

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: Famous spots like Keing Lay get packed on weekend evenings, and without a booking you may wait a while for a table. The oyster-farm rafts only do a few tables a day and depend on the weather — don't just drive out without calling to book, or you'll waste the trip.

faq.q: Are Ranong oysters really that big, and why are they famous?
faq.a: Yes. Ranong oysters are farmed in the brackish water right at the Kraburi estuary and Klong La-un, where fresh river water meets the salty Andaman. That mix is great for growing oysters, so they reach the size of your palm, with firm, bouncy meat and a sweet, faintly salty, non-fishy flavour.

faq.q: Where's the best place to eat raw oysters in Ranong?
faq.a: Keing Lay at Pak Nam is the one locals call the town's seafood legend — big fresh oysters with a waterfront view. If you want to shuck them fresh straight off a farm out at sea, head to the Farmer Boy oyster-farm raft at Klong La-un, but book ahead.

faq.q: Where should I go if I want fried or suan or don't dare eat raw oysters?
faq.a: Khun Lin and Somyot Pak Nam Seafood do or suan and oyster omelette well, with big oysters in crisp batter — a good option for anyone who'd rather not eat them raw.

faq.q: Roughly how much do oysters cost in Ranong?
faq.a: Eating at a normal sit-down restaurant runs around 150–500 THB per person depending on the place and how many dishes you order. The floating-farm dinner sets are 690–1,090 THB per person including the boat. If you buy shucked fresh oysters from the municipal market to cook yourself, it starts around 120–200 THB per 100g.

faq.q: What time of year is best for Ranong oysters?
faq.a: The dry season from around November to April — the sea is calm, the farms produce steadily, and it's easy to take a boat out to the floating farm rafts. In the rainy season the downpours are heavy and the sea rafts may close on some days, so call ahead to check.
